workspace._note: DISABLED 2026-06-15. The gemini-cli workspace server does its OWN Google OAuth outside jig's flow: a browser+localhost-callback path (works only on a local machine whose browser can reach the server's localhost) OR a headless copy-paste flow (show a Google URL -> user authorizes -> copies the credentials JSON Google returns -> pastes it back). On a deployed/headless host neither works as a plain clickable link, so re-auth fails (the connection shows green 'Connected' because a schema file exists, but the Google token is dead). Fixing it needs a custom in-dashboard paste flow we chose not to build: it'd serve only this 1-of-17 server (all others use jig's standard browser OAuth or a token command). To re-enable: remove this 'disabled' flag AND build that paste flow, OR keep it for local-only use. For Gmail on a deployed instance, use composio instead.

authoringHints: Use for email, calendar, drive files, documents, spreadsheets, and internal Google Workspace workflows.

github._note: DISABLED 2026-06-15. Use GitHub via composio instead. The remote GitHub MCP server (api.githubcopilot.com/mcp) does NOT support the app-free browser OAuth jig uses for every other remote server: GitHub's auth server has no Dynamic Client Registration (verified — github.com/login/oauth metadata has no registration_endpoint; jig connect errors 'Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration'). Per GitHub's own docs/host-integration.md, OAuth there requires a pre-registered GitHub App / OAuth App WITH a client_secret, which GitHub explicitly warns is unsafe to ship in a self-hosted/'uncontrolled environment' client like jig. The only no-secret OAuth path is device-flow with a registered app's client_id (custom code, not built). The PAT-header config below works but requires pasting a token. To re-enable: remove 'disabled' and either accept the PAT paste, or build the device flow. We chose composio.
github.setup: Paste a GitHub token. Create a fine-grained PAT at github.com/settings/tokens with read access to the repos, issues, and pull requests you want (a classic token with 'repo' scope also works).
